## Body

Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES
PR: #280
Head: ad27621c0f995aaf4cafcd9937257ebc84018c09
Request: 01a1f71c-498e-7990-ab1a-d08f12434451

Reviewed the complete six-file diff against 9ffc5729: crates/tmux/src/control.rs, crates/tmux/src/lib.rs, crates/tmux/tests/adapter.rs, crates/tmux/tests/control_mode.rs, docs/difficulties.md, and docs/how/macos-defender.md. Also inspected the public PR title/body and exact commit message. No dependency changes, identified credentials, new shell/path injection, or C21 forward-privacy violation were found.

S280-001 -- LOW, conditional availability residual; C34 follow-up, not a security block.
crates/tmux/src/control.rs:445-453 creates the directory and lock without an explicit private mode. File creation therefore depends on umask, and enclosing state directories are not guaranteed to be 0700 (crates/daemon/src/auth.rs:129-132,185-193 protects the credential file, not its parent).

Independent metadata-only checks observed state and pane-signals directories at 0755, a home ancestor at 0750, and a review-shell umask of 0022. The daemon umask and deployed default lock mode were not measured; that lock was absent. An inactive 0644 fixture lock accepted an exclusive flock through O_RDONLY. A second independently opened read-only descriptor was refused while the first held it and acquired it after release (one probe, exit 0). No file contents were read or changed.

If another UID can traverse every ancestor and read the lock, it can potentially hold the advisory lock indefinitely. That UID is outside C33. Group/ACL reachability and a different-UID exploit were not demonstrated, so this is a conditional residual, not a claim of compromise on this host. Follow-up: make the lock private without replacing its inode or introducing a lock-identity race. Same-user contention remains within C33.

Requested trace:

1. Lifetime: control.rs:346 acquires the named file guard before launch; :369-417 retains it through setup and ready-sentinel validation. It is not stored in Live or held for subsequent reads. Return paths and panic unwinding drop the guard; process death closes descriptors. Local Live cleanup (:188-192) runs before guard release on setup failure. Reader-thread creation failure at :368 precedes Live construction, so that exceptional child-cleanup path is not proof of synchronous kill/reap, although the attach guard still drops. The 3 s acquisition deadline begins after directory/file operations and is not a complete startup deadline.

2. Refusal and cost: control.rs:281-305 applies the 5 s restart backoff after startup fails. lib.rs:469-474,349-355 immediately forks an ordinary read when the control query returns None. Backoff limits startup attempts, NOT fallback forks. Sustained nominal 3 s contention plus 5 s backoff yields approximately one acquisition attempt per 8 s per adapter; the 10 ms wait retries at nominally 100 attempts/s while contended and launches nothing itself.

For P already-tracked panes with healthy pipes, the observer's control reads are one listing plus three reads per pane: owner (lib.rs:598-611), pipe state (:1170-1181), and capture (:1120). Under control denial this is 1+3P launches/pass, or nominally 1.67+5P launches/s at the 600 ms cadence, before blocking time. It is not a global maximum: other callers, repairs and writes add launches. No live-fleet launch-rate measurement was made by security.

3. Runtime: control.rs:456-459 sleeps synchronously. The observer is an ordinary tokio::spawn (crates/daemon/src/pane_observer.rs:206-214,247), and list_panes directly reaches the synchronous control query (lib.rs:872-875,469-473). HTTP spawn-session resolution also directly awaits it (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1521-1543). These paths do not hand the wait to a blocking pool. The revive-specific spawn_blocking at crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs:380-393 does not protect them. Security independently confirmed the source property, not a measured stall duration. Performance already recorded a BLOCK for this exact head (commit 58ca4c5d88cd4cbed072c586c283125aa34b5667); this security verdict does not clear that block or declare merge readiness.

4. Path confinement: control.rs:425-440 replaces characters outside ASCII alphanumeric, hyphen and underscore. A server label cannot escape the supplied root. Coordination is by root plus normalized label; normalization collisions are conservative over-serialization. The attach lock is a BRAKE: removing it permits more attaches, not a different answer policy.

- Separately executed correctness-review receipts were supplied and their complete written report inspected: PIJ_SHARED_TARGET="$(bash harness/scripts/cargo-target.sh)" just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-tmux passed 89 tests (27 unit, 41 adapter, 21 control-mode). A shared-build batch repeated the exact concurrent-attach sensor and reservation test 20 times each: both passed 20/20; the crash sensor covered 200 rounds. Removing only the acquisition guard in an isolated checkout, copying out the executable under the build lock, and running it at niceness 19 produced 20/20 mutant failures, exit 101, all server-death assertions. These are independently executed by the correctness reviewer, not security reruns.
- That reviewer's isolated current-thread Tokio diagnostic measured a first fallback read at 3.256 s and a separately armed 50 ms timer at 3.256 s. During backoff, 30 successful reads caused 30 fork launches in 959 ms and zero control-client launches. These are peer-observed diagnostic measurements, not sustained production-fleet measurements.
- Author-reported, not security-rerun: two-process driver 15/30 deaths without the lock versus 0/30 with it; concurrent-attach sensor 20/20 failing runs without versus 0/20 with; reservation test 0/100 failures with the lock. These are not independent security receipts.

No credentials were read, no live server was attached to or bounced, no source was edited, and no different-UID execution was performed.
